title: Runbook: Connection Error and Server Down Error, getSmeProxyState values and Tunnel 2.0 logs

prose.label: Tunnel 1.0 logs.
prose.text: {{tunnel-1-pac-parse}} {{tunnel-1-keepalive}} {{proxy-state-values}} What each status means is open {{gap:state-values-undefined}}.

meaning.statement: Client Connector shows a connection error when it fails to connect to Internet & SaaS or Private Access services because Zscaler data centers are unreachable; symptoms are the Internet Security window showing Connection Error or the logs showing Server Down Error, with intermittent or no internet access.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector shows a connection error when it fails to establish a connection to Internet & SaaS or Private Access services due to unreachable Zscaler data centers.
The Internet Security window displays Connection Error or the logs show Server Down Error.
Intermittent or no internet access.

log-keywords.statement: The Connection Error identification says to review Client Connector logs for PAC file parsing and connection attempts to gateway.<cloudname>.net, searching the keywords getSmeProxyState and Tunnel Forwarding Status.

quotes: Review Zscaler Client Connector logs for proxy auto-configuration (PAC) file parsing and connection attempts to gateway.<cloudname>.net.
Keywords to search: getSmeProxyState, Tunnel Forwarding Status.

tunnel-1-pac-parse.statement: For Tunnel 1.0 the runbook shows a ZSATunnel log where the app parses the PAC file and lists the primary and secondary data centers; in its sample the saved proxy string is PROXY 165.225.120.17:80; PROXY 165.225.122.17:80; DIRECT.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector parses the PAC file and lists the primary and secondary data centers:
INF Saving default proxy string as: PROXY 165.225.120.17:80; PROXY 165.225.122.17:80; DIRECT
PAC Parsing - ZSATunnel Log

tunnel-1-keepalive.statement: For Tunnel 1.0 the app monitors the primary proxy IP every 30 seconds; if keepalives fail with all data centers returned from the PAC file it goes into the connection error state, which can be followed by searching getSmeProxyState in ZSATunnel logs.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector performs monitoring for primary proxy IP every 30 seconds.
If the keepalives fail with all the data centers returned from the PAC file, Zscaler Client Connector goes into connection error state.
You can search for keyword getSmeProxyState in ZSATunnel logs to review the state of the connection over time.

proxy-state-values.statement: In the Tunnel 1.0 section, searching getSmeProxyState in ZSATunnel logs shows the connection state over time; the four statuses listed are TUNNEL_FORWARDING, CONNECTING, SERVER_DOWN_ERROR and LOCAL_PROXY_FORWARDING; the runbook's Endpoint Firewall or Antivirus Error section has ZApp Status log lines that also show getSmeProxyState:FIREWALL_BLOCK_ERROR.

quotes: Endpoint Firewall or Antivirus Error
DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:NON_TRUSTED getSmeProxyState:CONNECTING
getSmeProxyState:FIREWALL_BLOCK_ERROR getZpnProxyState:FIREWALL_BLOCK_ERROR
Here, you'll see four statuses: TUNNEL_FORWARDING, CONNECTING, SERVER_DOWN_ERROR, LOCAL_PROXY_FORWARDING.
You can search for keyword getSmeProxyState in ZSATunnel logs to review the state of the connection over time.

tunnel-2-channels.statement: Z-Tunnel uses DTLS or TLS to send packets to the Zscaler service; Tunnel 2.0 uses a control channel that is always TLS and a data channel whose protocol follows the Tunnel 2.0 mode set by Primary Transport Selection in the forwarding profile.

quotes: Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) has a tunneling architecture that uses DTLS or TLS to send packets to the Zscaler service.
The control channel is always on TLS protocol, and the data channel is according to the Tunnel 2.0 mode set on the forwarding profile selection Primary Transport Selection.

tunnel-2-state-log.statement: A Tunnel 2.0 ZSATunnel status line carries getSmeProxyState and a T2State block with Tx, Rx, IP, SME, Protocol and Status; one sample's Status holds ZSCCM:TUNNEL_FORWARDING and ZSDDC:CONNECTING.

quotes: T2State: [Tx:31109 Rx:29942 IP:10.254.120.171 SME:165.225.202.56 Protocol: DTLS Status:UP]
Status: ZSCCM:TUNNEL_FORWARDING ZSDDC:CONNECTING]
You can monitor the Tunnel 2.0 connection status by searching getSmeProxyState in Zscaler Client Connector ZSATunnel logs:

tunnel-2-fallback-log.statement: A Tunnel 2.0 fallback to Tunnel 1.0 is shown in the sample log by a connect timeout to 147.161.179.24:443 and the line 'SME List is empty. Fallback to ZTunnel 1.0'.

quotes: Tunnel 2.0 connection falling back to Tunnel 1.0 is highlighted in the following way:
Exception:Timeout: connect timed out: 147.161.179.24:443
SME List is empty. Fallback to ZTunnel 1.0

ssl-interception-log.statement: If a device intercepts SSL connections, the sample Tunnel 2.0 log shows ZST2M::ZT2A::initialize: Data Channel establishment Failed. and Auth::Lib::certificateErroCallback: Invalid certificate.

quotes: If any device intercepts SSL connections, it is highlighted with the following logs:
ZST2M::ZT2A::initialize: Data Channel establishment Failed.
Auth::Lib::certificateErroCallback: Invalid certificate

causes.statement: Possible causes listed are a network firewall or endpoint device blocking Zscaler IP ranges or specific ports, SSL interception or a network proxy interfering with Zscaler communication, and incorrect PAC file configuration.

quotes: Network firewall or endpoint device blocking Zscaler IP ranges or specific ports.
SSL interception or network proxy interfering with Zscaler communication.
Incorrect PAC file configuration.

udp-and-tls.statement: For Z-Tunnel 2.0 the runbook says to make sure UDP traffic is not restricted because Z-Tunnel 2.0 uses UDP for DTLS communication, and to switch the tunnel protocol to TLS and test.

quotes: For Z-Tunnel 2.0, make sure there is no restriction on UDP traffic as Z-Tunnel 2.0 uses UDP protocol for DTLS communication.
Switch the tunnel protocol to TLS and test if that helps improve the situation.

bypass-inspection.statement: Firewall or SSL interception devices should bypass Zscaler IP ranges, and traffic to gateway.<cloud_name>.net should be allowed on standard ports 80 and 443; the example PAC URL is http://pac.<cloud_name>.net/<cloud_name>.net/proxy.pac.

quotes: Firewall or SSL interception devices should bypass Zscaler IP ranges to prevent connection failures.
Allow traffic to gateway.<cloud_name>.net on all standard ports (80, 443).
http://pac.<cloud_name>.net/<cloud_name>.net/proxy.pac

state-values-undefined.title: What each getSmeProxyState value and the ZSCCM and ZSDDC status fields mean
state-values-undefined.detail: The runbook lists TUNNEL_FORWARDING, CONNECTING, SERVER_DOWN_ERROR and LOCAL_PROXY_FORWARDING as getSmeProxyState statuses without defining each (its Endpoint FW/AV sample also shows FIREWALL_BLOCK_ERROR, so the list of four is not the full set), and shows ZSCCM and ZSDDC in the T2State Status field without defining them.
